governing_table.code: Iowa State Plumbing Code, 481 IAC chapter 425: Uniform Plumbing Code with Iowa amendments. Iowa deletes the Uniform Plumbing Code's own Table 422.1 and inserts the International Plumbing Code's Table 403.1 in its place. The state building code's Chapter 29 is deleted (481 IAC 301.3(20)), so the plumbing code table is the only state table.
governing_table.edition: 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code, in force 2025-03-26 (IAC text read as published 2026-09-30). The inserted table is headed as reprinted from the 2018 International Plumbing Code.
governing_table.table: Table 422.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures (Iowa amendment 481 IAC 425.4(3)"i"; excerpt of 2018 IPC Table 403.1)
governing_table.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in each building for the type of building occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1 of the International Plumbing Code, reprinted here as Table 422.1. The design occupant load and occupancy classification shall be determined in accordance with the state building code or the authority having jurisdiction. Required public facilities shall be designated by a legible sign for each sex and signs be readily visible and located near the entrance to each toilet facility.
governing_table.statewide_quote: The provisions of the UPC, as adopted and amended by this chapter, are applicable to the plumbing in buildings or on premises in Iowa. Local jurisdictions may not adopt other plumbing codes. Local jurisdictions may adopt additional amendments provided they are stricter than the UPC as amended by this chapter and copies of any local amendments are provided to the board.
governing_table.note: The table header reads '(URINALS: SEE SECTION 422.7)'. In the 2024 UPC, 422.7 is Urinal Partitions; the substitution rule Iowa adds is numbered 422.8. Permits, inspection and enforcement are local (481 IAC 425.4(1)).

fixtures.cities_may_amend_note: Only with stricter amendments; a city may not adopt a different plumbing code (481 IAC 425.2).

office.row_label: 2 Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: No urinal column. Optional substitution under Iowa's added section 422.8: not more than 50% of the required water closets.
office.quote: 2 Business Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses | 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 | [lavatories] 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.urinals: No urinal column. Optional substitution under Iowa's added section 422.8: not more than 67% of the required water closets.
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts d | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | [lavatories] 1 per 200 | [drinking fountain] 1 per 500 | 1 service sink. Footnote d: The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required.

school.urinals: No urinal column. Optional substitution under Iowa's added section 422.8: not more than 67% of the required water closets.
school.quote: 3 Educational Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | [lavatories] 1 per 50 | [drinking fountain] 1 per 100 | 1 service sink

sex_split.text: Half male, half female, unless information submitted shows a different split. Iowa's amendment replaces only the first paragraph of 422.1, so 422.1.1 of the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code stays in force.
sex_split.quote: 422.1.1 Fixture Calculations. The minimum number of fixtures shall be calculated at 50 percent male and 50 percent female based on the total occupant load. Where information submitted indicates a difference in the distribution of the sexes such information shall be used to determine the number of fixtures for each sex.
sex_split.note: Read in IAPMO's free read-only edition of the 2024 UPC (page 36).

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number; any fraction of the stated number of people needs one more fixture. For mixed occupancies, sum the fractions first, then round.
rounding.quote: UPC 422.1.1: "Where applying the fixture ratios in Table 422.1 results in fractional numbers, such numbers shall be rounded to the next whole number. For multiple occupancies, fractional numbers shall be first summed and then rounded to the next whole number." | Iowa Table 422.1 footnote a: "The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated. The number of occupants shall be determined by the International Building Code."

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational uses and up to 50% in all other uses, including offices. Each urinal needs a partition on each side.
urinal_substitution.quote: 422.8 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies and not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies. (Reprinted from the 2021 International Plumbing Code section 424.2)

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate rooms for each sex are not required: in any occupancy with a total occupant load of 10 or fewer, or in a business or mercantile occupancy with a total of 50 or fewer (customers and employees), where one single-user toilet room serves both sexes; or where the room's fixtures are designed for both sexes and every toilet and urinal is in a privacy compartment.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 422.2 Separate Facilities. Separate toilet facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: (1) Residential installations. (2) In occupancies with a total occupant load of 10 or less, including customers and employees, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes. (3) In business and mercantile occupancies with a total occupant load of 50 or less including customers and employees, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes. (4) Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms have fixtures designed for use by both sexes and the water closets are installed in privacy compartments. Urinals shall be located in a privacy compartment.
small_occupancy_exception.note: 2024 UPC text (IAPMO read-only edition, page 36); Iowa's chapter 425 does not amend 422.2.

occupant_load.text: Office (business areas): 150 sq ft gross per occupant. Restaurant dining room (assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated, tables and chairs): 15 sq ft net. Classroom: 20 sq ft net. These are the state building code's figures (2024 IBC Table 1004.5); a city with its own building code uses that code's table.
occupant_load.quote: Iowa 422.1: "The design occupant load and occupancy classification shall be determined in accordance with the state building code or the authority having jurisdiction." | 2024 IBC Table 1004.5: "Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net [...] Business areas 150 gross [...] Educational Classroom area 20 net"
occupant_load.note: Table 1004.5 read on UpCodes' copy of the Iowa Building Code 2024 (secondary).

privacy.text: Every public toilet needs its own compartment with walls or partitions and a door. The 2024 plumbing code also names a product standard for partitions (IAPMO Z124.10): Type B security in separate-sex rooms, Type A in all-gender rooms, Type C for urinal screens. Urinal screens run from no more than 12 inches above the floor to at least 60 inches, and stand out at least 18 inches from the wall.
privacy.quote: 422.6 Water Closet Compartment. Public water closets shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. Partitions for water closets located in separate gender toilet or bathrooms shall comply with the Type B security requirements of IAPMO Z124.10. Partitions for water closets located in all gender toilet or bathrooms shall comply with the Type A security requirements of IAPMO Z124.10. [...] 422.7 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal shall be separated with walls or partitions to provide privacy. [...] Partitions for urinals shall comply with the Type C security requirements of IAPMO Z124.10. Walls or partitions shall extend from not less than 12 inches (305 mm) above the finished floor to not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor. Walls shall extend outward from the wall surface not less than 18 inches (457 mm).
privacy.note: Iowa's chapter 425 does not amend 422.6 or 422.7. IAPMO Z124.10 itself was not read: what Types A, B and C require of a partition is open.

worked_examples.how: 50 occupants split in half = 25 of each sex. 25/25 = 1, rounded up to 1 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 50% of the required men's toilets in a room: 50% of 1 = 0.5, so up to 0. With a total of 50 or fewer, a business occupancy may instead have one single-user toilet room used by both sexes.

100 occupants split in half = 50 of each sex. 50/25 = 2, rounded up to 2 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 50% of the required men's toilets in a room: 50% of 2 = 1, so up to 1.

200 occupants split in half = 100 of each sex. first 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 50/50 = 1, total 3, rounded up to 3 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 50% of the required men's toilets in a room: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so up to 1.

400 occupants split in half = 200 of each sex. first 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 150/50 = 3, total 5, rounded up to 5 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 50% of the required men's toilets in a room: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so up to 2.

50 occupants split in half = 25 of each sex. 25/75 = 0.33, rounded up to 1 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 67% of the required men's toilets in a room: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so up to 0.

100 occupants split in half = 50 of each sex. 50/75 = 0.67, rounded up to 1 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 67% of the required men's toilets in a room: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so up to 0.

200 occupants split in half = 100 of each sex. 100/75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 67% of the required men's toilets in a room: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so up to 1.

400 occupants split in half = 200 of each sex. 200/75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 67% of the required men's toilets in a room: 67% of 3 = 2.01, so up to 2.

50 occupants split in half = 25 of each sex. 25/50 = 0.5, rounded up to 1 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 67% of the required men's toilets in a room: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so up to 0.

100 occupants split in half = 50 of each sex. 50/50 = 1, rounded up to 1 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 67% of the required men's toilets in a room: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so up to 0.

200 occupants split in half = 100 of each sex. 100/50 = 2, rounded up to 2 for each sex. Urinals are optional and may replace at most 67% of the required men's toilets in a room: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so up to 1.

hdpe_fire.section: 2024 International Building Code Section 803.9, adopted without change in the Iowa State Building Code (481 IAC 301.3 lists no amendment to Chapter 8). It points to Section 803.1.1 (NFPA 286 room-corner test).
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP) Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286 Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1.
hdpe_fire.note: Section text read on UpCodes' copy of the Iowa Building Code 2024 (secondary); the absence of an Iowa amendment to Chapter 8 was read in the official rule. The state building code applies to state-owned and state-financed buildings and where a city or county has accepted it (Iowa Code 103A.12); a city with its own building code applies its own edition. City agent to confirm the city's edition.

access.state_standard: 481 IAC 301.18 (State Building Code, Part 2), statewide for buildings and facilities available to the public other than places of worship: comply with either the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design or Chapter 11 of the 2024 International Building Code and its other accessibility provisions (which reference ICC A117.1-2017 with Supplement 1). Iowa Code 103A.7(2)"e" requires the state rules to be 'consistent with federal standards for building accessibility'.
access.state_standard_quote: 481—301.18(103A,104A) Accessibility of buildings and facilities available to the public. Buildings and facilities that are available to the public, other than places of worship, shall comply with one of the following: 301.18(1) Applicable provisions of ADASAD 2010. 301.18(2) IBC, Chapter 11 and applicable accessibility provisions contained in IBC. Note: Approval of construction plans based upon compliance with the applicable provisions of the IBC, as provided, does not relieve the designer, builder, building owner, or building operator from responsibility under federal law to comply with all applicable provisions of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design.

differences.point: No mandatory state difference: the first option is the federal standard itself
differences.state: 481 IAC 301.18(1): "Applicable provisions of ADASAD 2010." 301.16(1): the rule "adopts the language of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design by reference".
differences.quote: Although rule 481—301.18(103A,104A) is based upon the federal 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design and adopts the language of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design by reference [...] determinations of state and local building officials charged with enforcement of these rules are not binding on other state or federal jurisdictions

differences.point: Vertical grab bar at the toilet (only where the project is designed to the building-code option, A117.1-2017)
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2017 604.5.1.2: a vertical grab bar 18 inches minimum, in addition to the 42-inch horizontal side-wall bar.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.5.1: "The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall." No vertical bar.
differences.quote: 604.5.1.2 Vertical Grab Bar A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.

differences.point: Number of accessible stalls (only under the building-code option)
differences.state: 2024 IBC 1110.2.4: at least 5 percent of compartments wheelchair accessible; where toilets plus urinals in a room total six or more, at least 5 percent ambulatory accessible in addition.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 213.3.1: "Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition to the compartment required to comply with 604.8.1, at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures."
differences.quote: 1110.2.4 Water Closet Compartment Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.

differences.point: Wheelchair stall door position (only under the building-code option; A117.1 gives a second option, so it is looser, and the stall must still meet the federal rule)
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2017 Table 604.9.3.1: front-partition door opening 56 inches minimum from the side wall closest to the toilet, or 4 inches maximum from the side wall farthest from it.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.8.1.2: "Where located in the front partition, the door opening shall be 4 inches (100 mm) maximum from the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet."
differences.quote: Front Wall or Partition From the side wall or partition closest to the water closet 56 inches (1420 mm) minimum or From the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet 4 inches (100 mm) maximum

differences.state: ICC A117.1-2017 604.10.2: "60 inches (1525 mm) minimum in depth and a width of 35 inches (890 mm) minimum and 37 inches (940 mm) maximum".
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.8.2.1: "Ambulatory accessible compartments shall have a depth of 60 inches (1525 mm) minimum and a width of 35 inches (890 mm) minimum and 37 inches (940 mm) maximum."
differences.quote: 604.10.2 Size The minimum area of an ambulatory accessible toilet compartment shall be 60 inches (1525 mm) minimum in depth and a width of 35 inches (890 mm) minimum and 37 inches (940 mm) maximum.

access.process: No separate state accessibility registration or review. The rule applies statewide to new construction and to renovations 'when local or state building codes require compliance with standards for new construction', and it is checked with the building plans: by the city or county building department where there is one, and by the state Building Code Bureau (Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing) for state-owned buildings, new buildings with state funding, licensed healthcare, assisted living and similar facilities; schools, colleges and child care centers go to the Bureau unless an approved local department reviews them. The Bureau's minimum plan review fee is $200. The federal ADA applies regardless.
access.process_quote: Rule 481—301.18(103A,104A) applies statewide to new construction of buildings and facilities available to the public and to renovation and rehabilitation projects on existing buildings and facilities when local or state building codes require compliance with standards for new construction. | Plan review page: "The Building Code Bureau always reviews state-owned buildings & healthcare facilities." "The minimum plan review fee is $200"
access.note: State rule read on the official IAC. A117.1-2017 and IBC Chapter 11 text read on UpCodes (secondary). Other A117.1-2017 changes (larger turning space and clear floor space in new buildings) were not read.

single_user.rule: The state plumbing code requires single-user toilet rooms and family or assisted-use rooms to carry a sign showing they may be used by either sex. One single-user room may serve both sexes in place of separate rooms where the total occupant load is 10 or fewer, or 50 or fewer in a business or mercantile occupancy. Iowa has no separate statute on single-user restroom signs for buildings in general. In schools, Iowa Code 280.33 lets a school designate a single-occupancy restroom for one sex, and lists access to a single or unisex single-occupancy restroom as an accommodation.
single_user.quote: 422.2.1 Single Use Facilities. Single use toilet facilities, bathing facilities, and family or assisted use toilet facilities shall be identified with signage indicating use by either sex. 422.2.2 Family or Assisted-Use Toilet Facilities. Where a separate toilet facility is required for each sex, and each toilet facility is required to have only one water closet, two family or assisted-use toilet facilities shall be permitted in place of the required separate toilet facilities.
single_user.note: 2024 UPC text, IAPMO read-only edition (page 37); not amended by 481 IAC 425.

all_gender_shared.rule: Allowed by the state plumbing code: separate rooms for each sex are not required where the room's fixtures are designed for both sexes, every toilet is in a privacy compartment and every urinal is in a privacy compartment. Partitions in an all-gender room must meet the higher (Type A) security level of the partition standard IAPMO Z124.10. The fixture count is the men's and women's numbers added together. Iowa's own amendment to 422.1 also says required public facilities 'shall be designated by a legible sign for each sex'; how a plan reviewer reads that sentence against the all-gender exception is not stated. Not allowed for multi-user rooms in schools (next item).
all_gender_shared.quote: 422.2 Exception (4): "Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms have fixtures designed for use by both sexes and the water closets are installed in privacy compartments. Urinals shall be located in a privacy compartment." | 422.1.1: "For toilet facilities designed for use by all genders, the minimum number of fixtures shall be the aggregate calculated at 50 percent female and 50 percent male in accordance with Table 422.1." | 422.6: "Partitions for water closets located in all gender toilet or bathrooms shall comply with the Type A security requirements of IAPMO Z124.10." | 422.7: "Urinals located in all gender toilet rooms shall be visually separated from the remainder of the room or each urinal shall be installed in a privacy compartment complying with Type A security requirements of IAPMO Z124.10." | Iowa 422.1: "Required public facilities shall be designated by a legible sign for each sex and signs be readily visible and located near the entrance to each toilet facility."

use_restrictions.rule: Schools only (public and nonpublic): Iowa Code 280.33 requires a school to designate every multiple-occupancy restroom or changing area for one sex, and bars a person from entering one that does not correspond with the person's sex. Iowa Code 216.9A makes this not a discriminatory practice. No statute was found that restricts restroom use in other government or private buildings. Iowa Code 4.1A (2025) says that distinctions based on sex in restrooms and locker rooms serve important government objectives and that 'separate accommodations are not inherently unequal'; it sets no restroom requirement itself. Since 2025 Acts chapter 1, the public accommodations section of the Iowa Civil Rights Act (216.7) lists sex and sexual orientation but not gender identity.
use_restrictions.quote: 280.33(2): "A school shall require a multiple occupancy restroom or changing area to be designated only for and used by persons of the same sex. A person shall not enter a multiple occupancy restroom or changing area, or a single occupancy restroom or changing area designated only for persons of the same sex, that does not correspond with the person's sex." | 280.33(1)"b": "'School' means a public school or nonpublic school." | 4.1A(3): "distinctions based on sex, including but not limited to in prisons or other detention facilities, domestic violence shelters, rape crisis centers, locker rooms, restrooms, and in other contexts where health, safety, or privacy are implicated resulting in separate accommodations, are substantially related to the important government objectives of protecting the health, safety, and privacy of the persons in these contexts."

public_wage.law: None. Iowa has no prevailing wage law for state, city, county or school construction. Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded or assisted work.
public_wage.quote: U.S. Department of Labor, Dollar Threshold Amount for Contract Coverage, footnote: "Twenty-four states do not have prevailing wage laws. These States are Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, New Hampshire, North Carolina, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota, Utah, West Virginia, Wisconsin."
public_wage.note: The Labor Department page refused a direct download (HTTP 403) and was read through the fetch tool, which returned the footnote in segments (the list as returned names 22 states). No Iowa state page saying so outright was found. Bills to create a state law have been introduced and not enacted (for example HF 478, 2025 session, per a search result; its bill history was not opened).

sales_tax.state_rate_quote: The state sales tax and use tax rates are the same. The rate is 6%. [...] In addition to the state sales tax, most local jurisdictions impose a local option sales tax. The rate is 1%. [...] There is no local option use tax.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable when delivered in Iowa. A seller with no physical presence in Iowa must collect Iowa sales tax, and local option tax, once it has $100,000 or more in gross revenue from Iowa sales in the current or prior calendar year. If the seller is not required to collect or does not, the buyer owes use tax at 6% (no local option use tax). A buyer owing $1,200 or more a year in use tax registers for a permit; others file the Non-Permit Use Tax Return.
shipped_goods.quote: The tax is imposed [...] when the tangible personal property or specified digital product is delivered in Iowa. [...] Ordinarily, the retailer is responsible for collection of the tax, but if the retailer is not required by law to collect the tax or the retailer fails to do so, the purchaser is then responsible for remitting use tax. [...] A retailer is not required by law to collect Iowa sales tax if the retailer does not have physical or economic nexus with Iowa, meaning the retailer has no physical presence in Iowa and has not generated $100,000 or more in gross revenue from sales into Iowa in the current or prior calendar year. | Remote sellers page: "Remote sellers must collect Iowa sales tax only if the remote seller has $100,000 or more in gross revenue from Iowa sales."

freight.rule: Delivery charges from the seller to the buyer are exempt if separately invoiced or separately stated on the bill. Freight folded into the price is taxed, and so is 'freight-in' (the seller's cost of getting the product from its own supplier), even if listed separately.
freight.quote: Freight, Shipping, and Handling Charges. Taxable: Inbound freight or freight-in charges do not fall within the definition of delivery charges, and are taxable when added to the price of a taxable retail sale. [...] Exempt delivery charges constitute the costs necessary to transfer the product from the seller to the purchaser. Exempt: If separately invoiced or separately stated on the bill | 701 IAC 219.14: "Transportation charges and delivery charges are not subject to the Iowa sales and use tax when they are separately contracted or, if no written contract exists, are separately itemized on the billing from the seller to the purchaser."
freight.note: Partitions shipped direct from a manufacturer to the job site: whether the Department treats that freight as delivery to the purchaser or as freight-in is for the seller's accountant or the Department.

install_labor.rule: It depends on the job. 'Carpentry repair and installation' is a taxable service in Iowa. The labor is exempt when it is on or connected with new construction, reconstruction, alteration, expansion or remodeling of a building. Labor on a repair or an installation that does not rise to that level is taxed at 6% plus local option tax. The Department's tests include the scope of the work and whether the item replaced was defective. The guidance does not mention toilet partitions.
install_labor.quote: Taxable services typically associated with the building trades include the following: Carpentry repair and installation [...] However, taxable labor charges are exempt when on or connected with new construction, reconstruction, alteration, expansion, or remodeling of buildings or other structures. Taxable labor charges remain subject to sales tax in all other instances, such as repairs and installations. [...] Is the item being replaced defective? For example, if a building's existing furnace is not defective, but the owner of the building has a new, more energy efficient furnace installed, the service is reconstruction or remodeling. However, if the building's furnace is defective, the replacement of the furnace is a repair. | 701 IAC 219.13: "Remodeling a building or other structure means much more than making repairs or minor changes to it." 219.13(6)"a": "Persons engaged in the business of carpentry, as the trade is known in the usual course of business, are selling a service subject to sales tax, regardless of whether they perform repair or installation."

furnish_and_install.rule: On new construction, reconstruction, alteration, expansion or remodeling, the contractor is the final consumer: the contractor pays sales or use tax on the materials when buying them and charges the customer no tax on materials or labor. On a repair or installation below that level, the contractor charges the customer tax on the materials and on any taxable labor. If the bill is not itemized, the whole amount is taxed. On a mixed job the bill must be itemized.
furnish_and_install.quote: When a contractor performs new construction, reconstruction, alteration, expansion, or remodeling, the contractor must pay sales or use tax on the building materials and supplies at the time they are purchased and does not collect any tax from the customer. Also, the contractor does not charge sales tax on the sales price of the labor involved in completing the job. In all other instances, such as repairs or installations that do not rise to the level of new construction, reconstruction, alteration, expansion, or remodeling, the contractor charges the customer sales tax on the sales price of the building materials and supplies used in completing the work. The contractor also charges the customer sales tax on the sales price of any taxable labor involved in completing the work.

sales_tax.note: All quotes from the Department's own guides (Contractors Guide dated 2025-08-27) and rule 701 IAC 219. Medium because none of them names toilet partitions: whether a partition replacement counts as remodeling or as a repair or installation, and whether partitions are building materials, is not stated.

page.stalls_intro: Iowa's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen.
page.stalls_after: An office or shop designed for 50 people or fewer may have one single-user restroom for everyone instead of separate rooms. A restaurant's seasonal outdoor seating counts toward its capacity. These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Iowa's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Iowa's state building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Those rules cover state buildings and the places that have adopted them, and a city with its own building code may use a different edition. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Iowa applies the federal sizes statewide, or lets a project follow the building code's own access chapter instead. Iowa has no separate state review for access: it is checked with the building plans, by the city or, for state buildings, by the state.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Iowa and federal stall rules match:** Iowa's access rules adopt the federal ones, so a stall that meets the federal sizes meets Iowa's. A project designed to the building code's access chapter instead also needs an 18 inch vertical grab bar beside the toilet. Iowa's plumbing rules also name a security standard for toilet partitions and urinal screens, so ask your plan reviewer whether it applies to your project.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must carry a sign showing that either sex may use it. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet and every urinal sits in its own privacy compartment. In public and private schools, Iowa law requires restrooms for more than one person to be designated for one sex.
page.public_jobs: Iowa has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on work paid for with federal money, where federal law sets it by county.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Iowa, installation labor is not taxed when it is part of new construction or a remodel, and a contractor who supplies and installs on that kind of job pays the tax when buying the partitions and adds none to the bill. Labor on a repair or a stand-alone installation is taxed. The state's guidance does not say which side a partition replacement falls on.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable. Delivery charges listed separately on the invoice are not. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Iowa Department of Revenue
sources: - Toilet counts in Iowa: [Iowa State Plumbing Code, 481 Iowa Administrative Code chapter 425](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/chapter/481.425.pdf) (2024 Uniform Plumbing Code with Iowa amendments: Section 422.1, Table 422.1 reprinted from the International Plumbing Code, and Section 422.8 on urinals), with the 50/50 split, rounding, separate-room exceptions and partition rules in Sections 422.1.1, 422.2, 422.6 and 422.7 of the [2024 Uniform Plumbing Code, IAPMO read-only edition](https://epubs.iapmo.org/2024/UPC/). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Floor area per person and the fire test for solid plastic partitions: [Iowa State Building Code, 481 Iowa Administrative Code chapter 301](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/chapter/481.301.pdf) (2024 International Building Code with Iowa amendments; Chapter 29 deleted, Chapter 8 unamended), Table 1004.5 and Section 803.9 read on a secondary copy of the [Iowa Building Code 2024](https://up.codes/viewer/iowa/ibc-2024/chapter/8/interior-finishes). Where the state building code applies: [Iowa Code 103A.12](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/103A.12.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Iowa access rules compared with the federal ones: [481 Iowa Administrative Code 301.16 to 301.18](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/chapter/481.301.pdf), the [2010 ADA Standards](https://www.access-board.gov/ada/), sections 213 and 604, and ICC A117.1-2017 sections 604.5 and 604.9 read on a [secondary copy](https://up.codes/viewer/iowa/icc-a117.1-2017/chapter/6/plumbing-elements-and-facilities). State plan review: [Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing, Building Code Plan Review](https://dial.iowa.gov/licenses/building/plan-review). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Restrooms in schools: [Iowa Code 280.33](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/280.33.pdf) and [216.9A](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/216.9A.pdf); see also [Iowa Code 4.1A](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/4.1A.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wages on public jobs: [U.S. Department of Labor, Dollar Threshold Amount for Contract Coverage](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/state/prevailing-wages) (Iowa listed among the states without a prevailing wage law). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax: Iowa Department of Revenue, [Sales & Use Tax Guide](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/sales-use-excise-tax/sales-use-tax-guide), [Iowa Contractors Guide](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/sales-use-excise-tax/iowa-contractors-guide) and [Remote Sellers & Marketplace Facilitators](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/sales-use-excise-tax/remote-sellers-marketplace-facilitators); [701 Iowa Administrative Code chapter 219](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/chapter/701.219.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

to_confirm: City agent (Des Moines): the city's own building code edition and amendments decide the floor area per person, the HDPE fire test and anything in Chapter 29 the city kept; the state plumbing table applies in every Iowa city, and a city may only add stricter plumbing amendments. Check Des Moines' plumbing amendments for any change to Table 422.1 or the urinal rule.
2024 IBC Table 1004.5, Sections 803.9, 1110.2.4 and 1210.3, and ICC A117.1-2017 were read on UpCodes (secondary), not on codes.iccsafe.org.

IAPMO Z124.10 (the partition security standard the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code names in 422.6 and 422.7: Type B for separate-sex rooms, Type A for all-gender rooms, Type C for urinal screens) was not read. Ask the manufacturers whether their partitions are listed to it, and the local plan reviewer or the Iowa Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board whether it is enforced.

Iowa's amended 422.1 says required public facilities 'shall be designated by a legible sign for each sex', while the unamended 422.2 exception (4) allows shared all-gender rooms: ask the local plan reviewer or the Iowa Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board how the two are read together.

The table header points to Section 422.7 for urinals, but Iowa's urinal substitution rule is numbered 422.8 (422.7 is urinal partitions in the 2024 code): a cross-reference slip in the rule, not a different rule.

Restroom laws: statutes were read in the 2026 Iowa Code (printed December 2025). Laws passed in the 2026 session were not checked one by one; one search found no new restroom law for government buildings. Recheck on legis.iowa.gov before launch.

Prevailing wage: the U.S. Department of Labor page was read through the fetch tool (direct download refused). No Iowa agency page states that the state has no prevailing wage law; confirm with the Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing, Labor division, if needed.

Sales tax: whether replacing toilet partitions is 'remodeling' (labor exempt, contractor pays tax on materials) or a 'repair or installation' (labor and materials taxed to the customer), and whether direct-shipped freight is an exempt delivery charge: Iowa Department of Revenue, 515-281-3114, or Abe's accountant. Local option tax (1%) depends on the address: city agent to read the rate for Des Moines.
State accessibility plan review for private commercial projects in places with no local building department was not found on the Bureau's page.
